sentences.text: The snout of this pterosaur is low, pointed, and curves upward.
A very tall bony crest abruptly juts out from the premaxillae, forming a crested wave with a concave leading margin.
The crest is flat along the midline of the upper jaw and has a fibrous texture that may indicate a horn sheath covering.
The teeth are robust, not very elongated, and extend to the very tip of the jaws.
The tooth count is five per premaxilla, at least nine per maxilla, and at least fourteen per dentary.
A ten-centimetre-long pterosaur fossil was discovered in 1993 by Jean-Jacques Lepage on the Normandy coast near Ecqueville.
Eric Buffetaut and colleagues named the genus Normannognathus with the type species N. wellnhoferi in 1998.
Normannognathus was initially classified in the family Germanodactylidae but recent analyses have placed it in various phylogenetic positions.
Normannognathus lived during the Kimmeridgian age of the Upper Jurassic in the Argiles d'Octeville Formation of France.
Normannognathus lived between 152.21 and 149.2 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian stage.
David Unwin considered Normannognathus to be a basal member of the Dsungaripteroidea in 2006.
Witton et al. concluded in 2015 that Normannognathus is an indeterminate monofenestratan, sharing characters with both ctenochasmatoids and non-pterodactyloid monofenestratans.
